game.name: Streets of Rogue
game.short_description: Fight, sneak, and hack your way through randomly generated cities. It's like Nuclear Throne meets Deus Ex, mixed with the anarchy of GTA. Rogue-lite meets immersive sim, and goes completely insane.

other_scores.score: no Metascore disclosed (5 and 3 critic reviews)

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Streets of Rogue (2017) is a unique roguelike where you pick from many characters and are dropped into small village-like levels full of mini quests and missions needed to reach the next area. He says each character changes play so drastically that each feels like its own game. The levels themselves are fairly repetitive and not very dense, and he worries that once every character is mastered it may get old. With about 15 hours played, he enjoys it a lot and places it around a mid B (transcript reads 'mid eight', likely 'mid B').
praise: Each character drastically changes how you play, like a different game
Lots of random events and mini quests per level
criticism: Random levels are not very dense
May get tiresome after finishing the game repeatedly with every character
unique_points: Character variety carries the game and masks repetitive level design
Small village-style areas with side missions required to progress
commentary.quote: every character is its own game almost
design_criteria: Character diversity: drastically different playstyles per character
Level design: random but sparse and repetitive
Replayability: many characters keep it fresh until all are mastered
Mission/quest structure: mini quests and required missions per area

community.one_liner: A top-down, procedurally generated action roguelite/immersive-sim hybrid by Matt Dabrowski (published by tinyBuild) where you pick from 20+ wildly different character classes and complete city-block missions by fighting, sneaking, hacking, bribing or causing chaos.
community.consensus_summary: Streets of Rogue is a player-beloved cult hit: Steam shows 'Overwhelmingly Positive' at about 96% of roughly 23,100 reviews, with sandbox freedom, character variety and co-op chaos cited over and over. Critics were also favourable but the critic sample is small (Metacritic lists 82 on Xbox One from 5 reviews and 75 on Switch from 4; PC Gamer gave 84). The game spent roughly two years in Early Access from 2017 and reached 1.0 on 12 July 2019 on PC, then Switch, PS4 and Xbox One. Criticism clusters around clunky melee and gun aim, RNG and unfair late-floor modifiers, weak build synergy compared with deeper roguelites, and a solo experience that some find repetitive. A sequel, Streets of Rogue 2, is still listed as 'coming soon' on Steam with no release date, and much of the recent review traffic is fans waiting for it.
best_things: Huge sandbox freedom: every mission has many solutions (stealth, hacking, bribery, violence, distraction, using gang rivalries) and the game lets you pick your own approach

20+ character classes that change how the game plays (cop gets XP for arrests, zombie turns kills into zombies, shapeshifter possesses NPCs, gorilla, scientist, politician, etc.), driving replayability
Emergent chaos from interacting systems: rival gangs, scientists vs gorillas, explosions, fridges and generators as weapons, NPCs reacting to each other and to you
Excellent co-op (local and online up to 4 players); widely described as better with friends
Humour and tone: absurd gags and parody factions are frequently called out by reviewers and players
Strong long-term content: big quests, mutators, DLC characters, Steam Workshop support, sandbox/custom levels and characters (one reviewer logged thousands of hours)
Responsive developer and unlocks earned in play rather than paywalled (Steam and Metacritic user reviews)
Music praised as fitting, though some want more tracks
worst_things: Clunky combat: melee described as flailing, gun shots sometimes lock onto unintended targets, and knockback when shot from several directions can be deadly
RNG-driven deaths: bad trait offers, unlucky items or a random NPC fight can end multi-hour runs
Late-floor modifiers (falling bombs, spreading goo, everyone armed with rocket launchers) are seen by some as unfair rather than fun
Heavy menuing to interact with things, and stealth and combat feel stiff to some players
Limited build depth/synergy compared with Gungeon-style roguelites, per a co-op reviewer

Technical gripes: Switch version lag (Metacritic user), Steam Deck unplayable per top negative review (controller inputs not recognised, sub-20 fps docked), occasional save-data loss and online multiplayer breakage reported in negative Steam reviews
Thin narrative; one player wanted story between levels and critics noted an abrupt, anticlimactic ending (DarkStation)
improvements: Tighter melee and aimed-gun handling, plus less knockback chaos
More build variety and stronger trait/item synergies so runs feel less like the same pool of offers
Better balance on later floors, with fewer arbitrary run-killers and unavoidable modifiers
Fixes and support for Steam Deck, controllers and online multiplayer stability
More side objectives and less downtime in co-op when one player finishes early; a cleaner split-screen UI with four players
More narrative or structure around missions and a more satisfying ending
unique_things: Roguelite structure (procedural floors, permadeath, unlocks) fused with immersive-sim style problem solving, often pitched as Nuclear Throne meets Deus Ex with GTA anarchy
Class-specific playstyles, objectives and roleplay hooks, so the 'who am I and why am I here' feel changes each run
Living simulated city where factions and NPCs fight each other independent of the player
Arcade-GTA-like top-down view with procedural city blocks, with a custom level, character and sandbox toolset
Drop-in local and online co-op and PvP in a game that otherwise feels like a solo sandbox
tedious_or_disliked: Waiting for useful traits to appear; some players feel the same weak offers recur
Long floors, especially in co-op, where finished players idle waiting for teammates
Repetition after the first dozen hours for players who don't chase new characters or big quests
Menu-heavy interaction and the death-count tracker (some find it demoralising)
Humour and writing that some find childish or annoying
divisive_points: Chaos vs fairness: fans love systems going haywire, detractors feel random NPC violence and modifiers make runs feel unfair
Best with friends vs solo: co-op is widely loved while some solo reviewers find it repetitive or shallow (mixed Switch critic score of 60)
Roguelite depth: many praise replayability via characters, others say build variety is thin
Sequel direction: Streets of Rogue 2 is more open-world, and some who tried its playtest felt it was going in a different direction
community.reception_notes: Metacritic figures are per platform: the headline 82 is the Xbox One Metascore from 5 critic reviews (Generacion Xbox 88; XboxAddict, DarkStation, TheXboxHub and GameSpew 80), user score 8.3 from 30 ratings; the Switch Metascore is 75 from 4 reviews. There is no PC Metascore on Steam's page. OpenCritic score could not be retrieved (web search budget was exhausted and the OpenCritic fetch returned the wrong game or no data), so it is left null. Wikipedia says the game entered Early Access in 2017 (Dabrowski began development in 2014, moving from Construct 2 to Unity) and released 1.0 on 12 July 2019. Sales: steam-revenue-calculator estimates about $3.26M gross / $0.96M net to the developer on Steam, and SteamSpy estimates 1-2M owners; these are rough Boxleiter-style estimates, not audited. Steam price is $19.99 and there is a soundtrack, a making-of and a character pack. Platform notes: Switch performance complaints, Steam Deck/controller issues per Steam reviews. Streets of Rogue 2 announced in 2020, still 'coming soon' with no date. Verification: Metacritic page re-fetched; Xbox One 82 (5 reviews), Switch 75 (4), PC and PS4 have no disclosed Metascore (5 and 3 reviews); user 8.3 from 30 ratings. The headline 82 is Xbox One only.
